title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
abstract: arXiv:2611.24051v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Result

translated_title: 注意力并非相关性：挑战自动驾驶中注意力的因果性
translated_abstract: 注意力已成为估计周围物体相关性和解释自动驾驶车辆驾驶决策的最广泛采用的解决方案之一。然而，其捕捉单个输入元素对AI模型输出因果影响的能力在文献中早已受到讨论，特别是在自然语言处理（NLP）领域。本工作将这一讨论引入自动驾驶领域，通过分析注意力在估计输入物体对自动驾驶车辆驾驶行为的影响（即其相关性）方面的准确性。为此，我们将不同的基于注意力的相关性估计方法与通过反事实分析获得的物体相关性因果参考进行对比。我们在超过80,000个合成驾驶场景上进行了分析，使用的自动驾驶车辆基于PlanT 2.0——一种最先进的基于Transformer的物体级规划模型。
tldr: 该论文通过将基于注意力的相关性估计方法与反事实分析获得的因果参考进行对比，在8万余个合成驾驶场景中验证了注意力并不能准确反映物体对自动驾驶决策的真实因果影响。
en_tdlr: This paper challenges the causality of attention in autonomous driving by comparing attention-based relevance estimation with counterfactual causal analysis across over 80,000 synthetic driving scenes, demonstrating that attention does not accurately capture the true causal relevance of objects to driving decisions.
